# 0054: Decision records pass the prose gates, and their shape may change while their argument does not

Status: accepted, 2026-09-29.
Refines [0047](0047-adrs-are-authored-as-data-and-their-markdown-is-generated.md) (ADRs are authored as data), whose argument still travels verbatim in substance.
The words of an accepted record may now be reshaped to pass the prose gates, with every claim unchanged.
Enforced by `make adrs-prose` in CI.

## Context

The prose gates (`@jpeakai/prose-gates`) check the mechanical subset of the repository's writing standard.
They flag mid-sentence line wraps, sentences over 25 words, em-dashes and lists disguised as prose.
The decision records had never been checked.
Their generated markdown carried 2,408 findings across 54 files.

Two rules stood in the way of fixing them.
`AGENTS.md` said an accepted record is never edited.
ADR 0047 said a record's argument travels verbatim from its authored `.yml` to its generated `.md`.
Both rules exist so a decision cannot be quietly rewritten after it was taken.
Neither was written to protect a line break or a 40-word sentence.

## Decision

**Every generated record passes the prose gates.** `make adrs-prose` regenerates the markdown and runs the gate, pinned to an exact version, over `docs/adrs/*.md`.
CI runs it beside `make adrs-check`, so a record that fails either gate fails the build.

**A finding is fixed in the `.yml`, never the `.md`.** The markdown is generated, so a fix made there is overwritten on the next `make adrs`.
The renderer's templates are fixed the same way, in `docs/adrs/templates/`.

**Shape may change; the argument may not.** An accepted record's words may be reflowed to one sentence per line.
A long sentence may be split into shorter ones.
An em-dash may become a comma, colon, parenthesis or full stop.
A list written as prose may become a bullet list.
No claim, number, date, name, code span, link or ADR reference changes.
A verbatim quotation of an outside source is split around, never inside.

**Anything beyond shape is still a new record.** Changing what a decision says, why, or with what consequence remains a superseding ADR.
The status-line cross-link remains the only other edit an accepted record takes.

## Consequences

The first pass reshaped every record.
The pinned gate's own safe fixes handled the line wraps and most em-dashes.
The long sentences were split by hand, shape only, and checked field by field.

A record now reads the way the rest of the documentation does.
A reviewer of a shape-only change checks one thing: that no claim moved.
`AGENTS.md` now forbids changing an accepted record's argument, instead of forbidding any edit.

## Lens

A record is kept for its argument, not its line breaks.
Hold the claims fixed and let the shape meet the standard every other document meets.
